metadata.title: मूल निवासियों के राजा की समाधी का जीर्णोद्धार होगा| Bir Biram Kishore Manikya's Samadi redevelopment
metadata.description: Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya Debbarman, born on August 19, 1908, in Tripura, was a prominent figure known as the "Modern Architect of Tripura." He was the son of Maharaja Birendra Kishore Manikya Bahadur Debbarman and ruled Tripura before its merger with India. Bir Bikram Kishore Debbarman is credited with initiating the modernization and development of Tripura during his reign. He established the first higher educational institution in the region and played a crucial role in the planning of present-day Tripura. His untimely death at the age of 39 in 1947 was a setback for the region's progress. Despite this, his contributions are honored through various institutions and landmarks, including Tripura Airport. However, his memorial site, Smadhi, had been neglected until recently. Tribal Welfare Minister Bikas Debbarma has pledged to revitalize the area within three months, showing respect to the tribal king's legacy and promoting the welfare of Tripuris.
